decisions.rationale: The artifact exists with the stated canonical URL, archive-http-fetch method, and Wayback finalUrl. The selected offsets are an exact contiguous extract in the retained MusicRadar artifact, in the Second Hand News section, and the extract directly supports Buckingham replacing McVie's bass part while McVie was on vacation with a simple quarter-note bassline and Caillat calling it the start of Buckingham calling the shots.

The sourceRef points to the same verified MusicRadar archive artifact and canonical URL. The offset extract is exact and contiguous within the Dreams section, and it supports Nicks writing in Sly Stone's Pit, emerging with Dreams, and Caillat making an eight-bar loop of Mick Fleetwood's playing for the hypnotic rhythm effect.

The artifact metadata and canonical source URL match the sourceRef, with the archive finalUrl present in the artifact. The exact contiguous extract is in the Never Going Back Again section and supports the Brushes working title, planned brushed snare roll, and restringing Buckingham's acoustic every 20 minutes to capture bright picking parts.

The sourceRef artifact and canonical URL match the archive-collected MusicRadar artifact. The contiguous offset extract appears in the Don't Stop section and directly supports Caillat saying it was Christine McVie's song, that her suggested duet with Buckingham improved it dramatically, and that the band kept changing the ending background vocals.

The artifact, canonical URL, and archive finalUrl are consistent with the sourceRef. The exact contiguous extract is in the Go Your Own Way section and supports the early acoustic-guitar beating and screaming context plus Caillat's statement that both solos were comped after giving Buckingham seven or eight tracks and sounded composed though they were not.

The sourceRef uses the verified MusicRadar artifact and canonical URL, with matching archive finalUrl in the artifact metadata. The offset-selected extract is exact and contiguous in the Songbird section, supporting the concert-recital approach at Zellerbach, Christine McVie onstage at a nine-foot Steinway, and Caillat using 15 piano tracks with two close mics and the rest distant.

The sourceRef metadata matches the single archive-http-fetched MusicRadar artifact and canonical URL. The selected extract is exact and contiguous within The Chain section, not borrowed from another track, and supports the first-song-worked-on statement, Christine McVie's Keep Me There origin, and Buckingham later connecting the parts by taking apart verses, playing Dobro, and asking Fleetwood for a straight quarter-note kick beat.

The artifact and canonical URL are the stated MusicRadar source with archive finalUrl recorded in the artifact. The exact contiguous extract is in the You Make Loving Fun section and supports the Yamaha electric piano origin, the Clavinet through wah-wah change, and Mick working the wah while Christine played.

The sourceRef artifactId and canonical URL match the archive-fetched MusicRadar artifact. The offset extract is exact and contiguous in the I Don't Want to Know section and supports Silver Springs being excluded because it was too long, the need for a shorter uptempo track, and the band cutting it without Nicks before she added vocals later.

The sourceRef points to the verified archive-http-fetched MusicRadar artifact and canonical URL, with the artifact finalUrl present. The exact contiguous extract is in the Oh Daddy section and supports Caillat's early-session timing after The Chain, Christine on organ, Lindsey on guitar with Caillat's qualified Strat recollection, and Rick Turner's Stratoblaster boost device being used for edgier sound.

The MusicRadar sourceRef uses the verified artifact and canonical URL. The offset extract is exact, contiguous, and in the Gold Dust Woman section; in that named-track context it supports the 10-to-12-minute, many-verse inception, Caillat's editing down of sections, and Nicks objecting because particular verses or parts had personal meaning.

The sourceRef artifactId and canonical URL match the actual archive-http-fetched MusicRadar artifact. The selected offsets are exact and contiguous in the Gold Dust Woman section, distinct from the prior Gold Dust Woman fact, and support Nicks's coyote-like howling at the end and Fleetwood breaking glass in a miked room to accentuate her vocals.
